Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for West Indies' reply. The Indians break from their huddle and make their way out to the centre. It will be Qiana Joseph and Hayley Matthews to open the innings for West Indies. Renuka Singh Thakur will kickstart proceedings with the new ball for India. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

This will take some doing for the West Indies, who were far from their best with the ball and in the field. Their highest successful run chase in T20Is is 213, so they have chased a 200-plus total before. However, adding to the challenge, the highest successful chase at this venue in women’s T20Is is 173, making this chase historic if they manage to pull it off. With the dew coming in, India will have to bowl well to defend this total. Back in a bit for the second essay.

Although Rodrigues was the first to fall, followed by Mandhana, the Indian innings maintained its momentum. This was made possible due to a blistering 70-run stand off just 32 balls between Raghvi Bist and Richa Ghosh, who ensured there were no quiet overs and kept the scoreboard ticking until the end. Ghosh was particularly sensational, bringing up her fifty off just 18 balls, joining Sophie Devine and Phoebe Litchfield as the record holders for the fastest T20I fifty.

Well, India have turned up in the decider, haven't they? 56 runs off the last 4 overs have propelled the hosts to 217, their highest T20I total in women's cricket. After opting to bowl first, West Indies started strongly with Chinelle Henry striking early to deliver a disciplined opening over. However, they couldn't build on that scalp as Smriti Mandhana took charge, smashing her way to a third consecutive fifty. Jemimah Rodrigues complemented her perfectly, and together they took the attack to the opposition.

FOUR! BANG! A powerful end to the innings by Sajana S. Full and at the stumps. Sajana S drills this to the right of long off and it gets to the boundary in a flash. India Women finish with a mammoth score of 217/4.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Hayley Matthews to Jemimah Rodrigues, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Turning away, shorter in length, near the tramline on off, Smriti Mandhana pats it wide of cover for one more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Hayley Matthews to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Aerial but safe! Tossed up, full and on middle, Jemimah Rodrigues gets down for the sweep but fails to keep the shot along the ground. It goes on the bounce to the deep backward square leg fielder. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Hayley Matthews to Jemimah Rodrigues, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nicely tossed up, on a nagging length, around off, Jemimah Rodrigues clips it to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Hayley Matthews to Jemimah Rodrigues, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Matthews starts with a low full toss, at the stumps, Jemimah Rodrigues sweeps it fine to the right of deep backward square leg for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Hayley Matthews to Jemimah Rodrigues, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Hayley Matthews comes into the attack.
Pushed across the batter again by Dottin, on a length, left alone by Mandhana.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Deandra Dottin to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Not in control but Mandhana gets away with it! Angling across the left-hander, on a good length, outside off, Smriti Mandhana goes for the drive with hard hands and the ball flies off a thickish outside edge. It clears the leaping backward point fielder for four more runs. 20 runs off the over so far.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Deandra Dottin to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Too short and Mandhana climbs all over it! A half-tracker, on off, Smriti Mandhana lets the ball come to her and nails the pull through mid-wicket for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Deandra Dottin to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Shot of the night so far! Fuller in length, on off, Smriti Mandhana stays leg side of the ball and crouches to make the connection. Goes inside out over cover and clears the fence for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Deandra Dottin to Smriti Mandhana, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Short and punished! Banged in short by Dottin, over middle, Smriti Mandhana goes deep in the crease and pulls it aerially, beating deep mid-wicket to her left for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Deandra Dottin to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Had the throw hit, it would have been interesting! On a back of a length, on middle, Jemimah Rodrigues gets on the back foot and tucks it to the right of mid-wicket. Sets off for the single and it is a wayward throw from Hayley Matthews at the bowling end, allowing Jemimah to make her ground.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Deandra Dottin to Jemimah Rodrigues, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Slipping down leg, on a length, Jemimah Rodrigues gets inside the line for the tickle but misses. Half a shout for caught behind but the umpire signals a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Deandra Dottin to Jemimah Rodrigues, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Make that a hat-trick of boundaries! The length is pulled back now but Henry offers a bit of width on off, Smriti Mandhana waits on the back foot and cuts it between point and cover for yet another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Chinelle Henry to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Two in two for Mandhana! Good-length delivery, on off, Smriti Mandhana takes a couple of steps down the track and gets her hands through the line of the ball to loft it over mid off for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Chinelle Henry to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Mandhana connects this time and finds the fence! A bit too straight, on a back of a length, at the hips, Smriti Mandhana gets inside the line and pulls it nicely. Beats the diving deep backward square leg fielder to her right for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Chinelle Henry to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Shaping back into the left-hander, on a good length, Smriti Mandhana swivels to pull it by using the swing and the angle. The ball goes under her angled bat and hits her on the right thigh.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Chinelle Henry to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: At the stumps, on a nagging length, Jemimah Rodrigues gets on her toes and pulls it to deep backward square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Chinelle Henry to Jemimah Rodrigues, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: In that probing channel on off, shaping away, on a length, Jemimah Rodrigues walks across and gets behind the line to push it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Chinelle Henry to Jemimah Rodrigues, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: At 110.5 kph, this kicks up a bit, on middle and leg, on a back of a length, Smriti Mandhana walks down the track to smear it away on the leg side. Gets taken aback by the lift off the deck. Wears it high on the thigh pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Deandra Dottin to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Going across the batter from over the wicket, on a short of a length, Smriti Mandhana gets on top of the bounce and punches it to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Deandra Dottin to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Classy shot! On a good length, in the channel on off, Smriti Mandhana stays leg side of the ball and plays it right under her eyes. Punches it to the right of the diving cover fielder for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Deandra Dottin to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Slanting into the pads, on a back of a length, Jemimah Rodrigues nudges it through square leg and gets off the mark with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Deandra Dottin to Jemimah Rodrigues, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: At 107.4 kph, on a back of a length, Smriti Mandhana swivels to pull it away but the ball comes on slower than she expected. Ends up dragging it off the toe-end of the bat to square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Deandra Dottin to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dottin starts with a full delivery, shaping away, on off, Smriti Mandhana firms the drive to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Deandra Dottin to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Deandra Dottin will share the attack from the other end. Jemimah Rodrigues walks in at 3 for India Women.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND GONE! An ideal end to a disciplined first over for Henry! Henry bowls it on middle and leg, full in length, Chetry takes the risk of clipping it off the pads with the ball swinging away from her. She closes the bat face early and gets a leading edge that goes straight up towards cover where Qiana Joseph settles under it and does the rest.
Commentary.Howout: c Qiana Joseph b Chinelle Henry
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Chinelle Henry to Uma Chetry, OUT! c Qiana Joseph b Chinelle Henry.

Commentary.Commentary: From over the wicket to the right-hander, a hint of nibble away, on the fuller side, on the off-stump line, Chetry squeezes it out off the outer half of the bat towards cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Chinelle Henry to Uma Chetry, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched up by Henry, outside off, Smriti Mandhana shapes up for the drive but gets an inside edge down to deep fine leg for a single. Mandhana and India are underway in a streaky fashion!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Chinelle Henry to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, that could have so easily trickled back onto the stumps! On a back of a length, on middle and leg, Smriti Mandhana swivels to pull it away but the ball catches her on the glove and rolls past the leg stump.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Chinelle Henry to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Swinging back in again, at the stumps, on a length, Smriti Mandhana walks down the track to negate the movement. Ends up mistiming the drive back to Henry.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Chinelle Henry to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Henry gets a good inward shape as she steams in from around the wicket, on a length, on the off-stump line, Smriti Mandhana covers the line of the ball and pushes it to the right of the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Chinelle Henry to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the action to commence. Hayley Matthews and Co. are in a huddle near the ropes before taking their respective positions in the field. A loud cheer from the crowd greets the two Indian openers, Smriti Mandhana and Uma Chetry. Chinelle Henry will start with the new ball for West Indies. The countdown is done and dusted. Off we go...

PITCH REPORT - Shebani Bhaskar informs that this is the same pitch which was used in the first two games. Mentions that there is less grass as compared to the first game. Feels that there will not be much deterioration and this deck looks good to bat on. Adds that since it is the third game on the same surface, it could be on the slower side.

The stand-in skipper of India Women, Smriti Mandhana says that they would have bowled first as well but it is now about putting a good total on the board. Feels that anything above 185 will be a good total. States that they are ready to do whatever it takes to get the win. Mentions that the fresh faces in the team have looked positive and have brought good energy to the dressing room. Informs that they are going unchanged for this game.

The captain of West Indies Women, Hayley Matthews says that she has been pretty lucky with the toss and informs that they will bowl first. Feels that the conditions suit bowling first. Shares that the talk has been about executing the plans and she is glad that they were able to do well in the last game. Informs that they have made one change with Aaliyah Alleyne coming in for Ashmini Munisar.

West Indies Women (Playing XI) - Hayley Matthews (C), Qiana Joseph, Shemaine Campbelle (WK), Deandra Dottin, Chinelle Henry, Nerissa Crafton, Shabika Gajnabi, Zaida James, Afy Fletcher, Karishma Ramharack, Aaliyah Alleyne (In for Ashmini Munisar).

India Women (Unchanged Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana (C), Uma Chetry, Jemimah Rodrigues, Raghvi Bist, Richa Ghosh (WK), Sajana S, Deepti Sharma, Radha Yadav, Saima Thakor, Titas Sadhu, Renuka Singh Thakur.
TOSS - West Indies Women have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

As for the West Indies, their emphatic win in the second T20I ended a streak of nine consecutive losses against India in this format. The top order, led by Hayley Matthews, displayed impressive intent, comfortably chasing down the target and giving the team a much-needed confidence boost. On the bowling front, it was Deandra Dottin who stood tall in keeping the hosts in check. Fielding has been an issue for both sides, particularly for the visitors, and they will need to tighten up in that department. Buckle up, this promises to be a cracker of a contest. Stick around for the toss and team news.

For the hosts, Smriti Mandhana has been the linchpin of the batting lineup, delivering back-to-back fifties. While Jemimah Rodrigues shone in the series opener, the rest of the batting unit has yet to step up. India will be hoping for the return of skipper Harmanpreet Kaur, who missed the previous game due to a knee niggle. The bowling unit struggled to respond strongly when put under the pump in the last game, and a collective improvement will be key to their chances in this crucial encounter.

Hello and welcome to the T20I series decider between India Women and West Indies Women at the Dr. DY Patil Sports Academy in Navi Mumbai. The series has been a rollercoaster so far, with India striking first to seize the early advantage, only for Hayley Matthews and her spirited team to bounce back in style.
... MATCH DAY ...

It’s all even-stevens in this thrilling T20I series between India Women and West Indies Women after two entertaining matches that went either ways. After India dominated the series opener, West Indies bounced back with an impressive victory in the second game, setting up an enticing winner-takes-all clash. The hosts have been grappling with the absence of regular captain Harmanpreet Kaur, who missed the previous match due to injury. Her availability for the decider remains uncertain. While Smriti Mandhana and Richa Ghosh showed promising form with the bat in the last game, the rest of India's batting lineup struggled to make an impact. The bowling department's lackluster performance was particularly concerning, as they failed to contain the West Indies batters effectively. Smriti Mandhana in particular has led from the front and has notched up back-to-back fifties to her name, and she also happens to be the only player across both sides to have crossed the triple figures in the series. While Jemimah Rodrigues has provided valuable support, the team needs more players to rise to the occasion. The management has experimented with the lineup, giving opportunities to newcomers Uma Chetry as opener and introducing Raghvi Bist to international cricket. However, India's bowling has emerged as a significant concern, delivering underwhelming performances in both matches. Though Titas Sadhu and Radha Yadav have shown promise, Renuka Singh Thakur and Saima Thakor are still finding their rhythm. The team is also looking for seasoned all-rounder Deepti Sharma to make a bigger impact in the series. The West Indies camp draws confidence from their recent victory, powered by a stellar all-round display from Hayley Matthews. She excelled first with her bowling and then produced an explosive batting performance, finding excellent support from opening partner Qiana Joseph and later Shemaine Campbelle. However, despite securing the win, the Caribbean side has room for improvement. Their fielding performance remains a particular concern, having dropped four catches in the previous match, an area they'll be eager to address and make amends. The bowling attack remains largely dependent on Matthews and Dottin and the others need to gear up to support the two stalwarts. Though Chinelle Henry and Afy Fletcher have displayed flashes of good performances, they would be keen to keep up with the consistency. Will West Indies Women take the series, or can hosts India Women mount a comeback? It’s going to be a humdinger of a contest, folks!
